setup.title: Getting started
setup.lede: Four steps make your server ready: the domain, a secure connection, a chat and your first site. This page checks them for you.
setup.ready.text: Everything works. You can hide this checklist now.
setup.checked: Checked at {time}. The results are kept for a minute.
setup.checking.text: Looking up the domain and the secure connection. It takes a few seconds.
setup.hide.hint: You can bring it back in Settings.
setup.hidden: The checklist is hidden. It is in Settings if you need it again.
setup.shown: The checklist is back in the menu.
setup.hidden.note: The Getting started checklist is hidden from the menu.
setup.domain.title: Point your domain to this server
setup.domain.lede: Checking that {domain} and its sub-addresses lead to this server.
setup.domain.done: {domain} and every address under it lead to this server.
setup.domain.reason.no_records: {domain} does not lead anywhere yet. Add the two records below where you bought the domain.
setup.domain.reason.apex_missing: Sub-addresses work, but {domain} itself does not lead anywhere yet. Add the “@” record below.
setup.domain.reason.wildcard_missing: {domain} works, but addresses under it (like api.{domain} and your sites) do not yet. Add the “*” record below.
setup.domain.reason.points_elsewhere: The domain leads to another server, probably an old hosting. Change the records to the values below.
setup.domain.reason.lookup_failed: The domain could not be looked up just now. Check again in a minute; if it repeats, check that the domain is paid and active.
setup.domain.reason.ips_unknown: {domain} and its sub-addresses lead to a server. This server does not know its own public address, so it trusts the next step: if HTTPS works, the domain is right.
setup.domain.where: Open the DNS settings where you bought the domain and create these records:
setup.domain.col.name: Name
setup.domain.value.unknown: your server’s IP address (your hosting provider shows it)
setup.domain.names: “@” means the domain itself; “*” means every address under it: api and all your sites.
setup.domain.sub: If {domain} is part of a bigger domain (for example sites.example.com inside example.com), type the names relative to it: sites instead of @ and *.sites instead of *.
setup.domain.wait: Changes usually work within minutes, sometimes a few hours. Then press “Check again”.
setup.domain.ipsunknown: The installer normally fills in the address. If you set up the server by hand, ask whoever did it for the server’s public IP address.
setup.https.title: Secure connection (HTTPS) works
setup.https.lede: Checking that {host} opens over HTTPS with a valid certificate.
setup.https.done: {host} opens over HTTPS with a valid certificate.
setup.https.reason.dns_pending: Waits for the first step: the certificate is issued automatically once the domain leads here.
setup.https.reason.cert_invalid: {host} answers, but its certificate is not valid yet. Certificates are issued automatically a few minutes after the domain starts leading here: check again in 5 minutes.
setup.https.reason.unreachable: This server could not open {host}. Check that ports 80 and 443 are open in your hosting provider’s firewall, then check again.
setup.https.reason.bad_status: {host} answers with an error (code {status}): the web server works, but dropsite behind it does not respond. Wait a minute and check again; if it repeats, restart the server.
setup.https.limit: If it still fails after an hour: Let’s Encrypt issues at most 50 certificates a week for one domain. When many addresses were opened while the domain was not ready, wait until the next week.
setup.chat.title: Connect ChatGPT or Claude
setup.chat.todo: Connect a chat once, then make and change sites by simply asking.
setup.chat.done: A chat or a program is connected to your account.
setup.site.title: Make your first site
setup.site.todo: Ask the chat “make a site for my coffee shop and publish it”, or create a site here and upload its files.
setup.team.title: Invite a teammate
setup.team.todo: Give a colleague their own login: they get their own sites and can connect their own chat.
setup.team.done: Someone else uses this server too.
setup.requests.title: Get requests in Telegram or by e-mail
setup.requests.todo: Connect a Telegram bot or a mail server once, so site owners can receive form requests there.
setup.requests.done: Requests can be sent to Telegram or by e-mail.
connect.guide.gpt.1: Open **chatgpt.com** in a browser, click your name at the bottom left and choose **Settings**.
connect.guide.gpt.2: Open **Apps**, then **Advanced settings**, and turn on **Developer mode**.
connect.guide.gpt.3: Go back to **Apps** and press **Create app**.
connect.guide.gpt.4: In **Name** type dropsite. In **MCP Server URL** paste this address:
connect.guide.gpt.5: In **Authentication** choose **OAuth**, tick the box that you trust this app and press **Create**.
connect.guide.code: A dropsite page opens and asks for a code. Come back here, press **Connect** in step 02, type the code on that page and press **Allow**.
connect.guide.gpt.7: Start a new chat, press **+**, then **More**, and pick **dropsite**. Now write your request.
connect.guide.claude.1: Open **claude.ai** or the Claude Desktop app, click your name at the bottom left and choose **Settings**.
connect.guide.claude.3: In **Name** type dropsite. In **Remote MCP server URL** paste this address:
connect.guide.claude.4: Press **Add**, then press **Connect** next to dropsite.
connect.guide.claude.6: In a chat, press **+** under the message box and check that **dropsite** is turned on. Claude Desktop gets the connector too.
connect.guide.claude.team: On a Team or Enterprise plan the owner first adds the connector in **Admin settings** → **Connectors**.
connect.first.title: What to say first
connect.first.check.text: If the chat answers with your list (it may be empty), the connection works. Then ask for what you need, for example:
connect.first.make: “Make a one-page site for my bakery with a contact form and publish it”
connect.trouble.title: If something does not work
connect.trouble.dns.q: The chat says it cannot reach the server
connect.trouble.dns.a: The domain is probably not ready yet: it must lead to this server and open over HTTPS.
connect.trouble.checklist: Check it on the Getting started page →
connect.trouble.askadmin: Ask your administrator to finish the server setup.
connect.trouble.failed.q: “Connector failed” or “could not determine OAuth settings”
connect.trouble.failed.a: Open this address in your browser:
connect.trouble.failed.b: It must show text that starts with “{”. If it does not open or the browser warns about the certificate, the secure connection is not ready yet.
connect.trouble.plan.q: ChatGPT has no Developer mode or Create app
connect.trouble.plan.a: Custom apps work only on some ChatGPT plans, and in a work or school workspace an admin has to allow them. Ask them, use **Claude** instead, or check the current terms:
connect.trouble.code.a: A code works once and for 10 minutes. Press **Issue a new code** in step 02 and type the new one.
connect.trouble.unused.q: The chat answers, but does not make the site
connect.trouble.unused.a: Check that **dropsite** is turned on in this chat (step 7 for ChatGPT, step 6 for Claude) and add “use dropsite” to your request.
